newsitem.title: USA: NRC ratings decline at Kansas nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: NRC ratings decline at Kansas nuclear plant.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission's (NRC) performance report for Wolf Creek Nuclear Operating Corporation showed a decline in ratings in three of four categories, the corporation said Friday.

The NRC's Systematic Assessment of Licence Performance (SALP) report awards ratings in four areas: plant operations, plant support, maintenance and engineering. The report rates performance as either "superior," "good" or "acceptable."
Wolf Creek earned a "good" rating in plant operations, plant support and maintenance, while engineering was given a rating of "acceptable," the corporation said.
Wolf Creek's previous SALP report was issued in November, 1995, when the operations and plant support areas were rated "superior" and maintenance and engineering were rated "good."
The most recent SALP report covers performance between October 8, 1995 and April 5, 1997.

"(The report) underscores the need for improvement in our corrective action program. Even before the report was issued, we had taken measures to improve our corrective action program," WCNOC president and chief executive Otto Maynard said in a statement.
NRC officials will review specifics of the report at a public meeting scheduled May 22 at Wolf Creek.

Wolf Creek Generating Station is located near Burlington, Kansas. The plant is owned by Kansas City Power and Light Co, Kansas Electric Power Cooperative Inc (KEPco) and KGE, a unit of Western Resources Inc.
